page: Amazon Web Services m6i.2xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by a 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The processor features 54 MB of L3 cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 with VNNI, AES, and SHA-NI cryptographic acceleration. The instance is configured with 32 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4 GB per virtual core. Local storage is not bundled, and network capability is provisioned at a 3 Gbps baseline bandwidth without complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations position the m6i.2xlarge within average performance percentiles across general compute, memory, and application-level workloads. It registers a Geekbench single-core score of 1638.0 and a multi-core score of 6013.0, paired with a PassMark CPU composite score of 11434.57. Large-block memory tests demonstrate read throughput of 58.41 GB/sec and write throughput of 42.0 GB/sec. Operational throughput benchmarks record 7.98 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks and 11.87 GB/sec in static web serving. In contrast, heavier computational pipelines reveal limitations; multi-threaded bzip3 decompression yields 30.92 GB/sec falling into the lower quartile, and CPU-based medium (7B) language model inference is constrained at 7.74 generation tokens per second due to the lack of dedicated GPU hardware.

From a cost efficiency standpoint, the m6i.2xlarge offers balanced resource density without the pricing overhead of specialized accelerator silicon or excessive memory tiers. Because the instance contains no local NVMe storage, persistent storage and high-throughput IOPS depend on external network-attached volumes. This architecture suits steady-state production environments including mid-sized relational databases, microservices hosting, enterprise web backends, and continuous integration and deployment pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services m6i.2xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose instance featuring an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz on the AWS Nitro platform. It provides 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores, 32 GB of DDR4 memory at 3 GHz, and a 3 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance includes no bundled local storage and no GPU accelerators. Performance metrics demonstrate dependable mid-tier capabilities, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 6013.0, 7.98 million Redis SET operations per second, and 11.87 GB/sec static web serving throughput. While complex multi-threaded decompression and CPU-based AI inference represent architectural bottlenecks, the balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM configuration delivers predictable resource density. It is well suited for medium-tier enterprise backends, container orchestration nodes, relational database workloads, and application server hosting.
